title: Degasser Tower

introduction.definition: A forced-draught degasser (decarbonator) removes dissolved CO₂ from water, usually after a cation exchanger. Water is spread over packing and trickles down while a blower sends air up; the CO₂ moves from the water into the air (which contains almost none) and is vented. Degassed water collects in the sump below.
applications: Between cation and anion units in DM plants
After acid dosing ahead of RO; groundwater CO₂/H₂S stripping
key_points: Henry's law: gas leaves water when air has little of it

pressure.title: CO₂ concentration falls down the tower
pressure.description: After cation exchange, bicarbonate has turned into dissolved CO₂ (carbonic acid). Air blown up through the packing strips it out (Henry's law: the air has almost no CO₂), typically down to ~ 5 mg/L, which greatly reduces the load — and regenerant use — on the anion exchanger.

video_tutorials.title: Degasser Tower — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Degasser Tower.
Check blower and sump level.
Inspect distributor and packing.
Replace packing if fouled.
Watch for high co₂ outlet: anion runs short. Common cause: blower failure, channelling.
Watch for packing fouling: high δp. Common cause: biological growth.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
